A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original coupled-matrix experiments and CP-completion experiments on real and synthetic tensors in Section 5 and Appendix B, including Figures 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and results in Section 5 and Appendix D, including Figures 1–3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the CP/Tucker/TT reductions and the adaptive-step acceleration procedure are unchanged. Appendix A.4 discusses further applications of the existing approach without introducing new algorithmic steps.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same coupled-matrix problem, CARDIAC-MRI, HYPERSPECTRAL, RANDOM-CP and RANDOM-TUCKER tensors. Newly discussed decomposition families are not experimentally evaluated.

E2.justification: The coupled-matrix comparison retains direct, mini-als and approximate-mini-als. CP comparisons retain direct, the Tomasi–Bro parafac method, mini-als and accelerated-mini-als. The parafac naming cleanup does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Dataset dimensions, masking, initialization, rank and observation-rate sweeps, sampling fraction and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. v2 omits the seven-iteration disclosure rather than specifying a replacement budget; this is a documentation loss, not an established protocol revision.

E4.justification: The rank, tolerance and observation-rate sweeps and acceleration comparisons in Figures 2–3 are retained. The expanded coupled-matrix discussion interprets existing evidence without adding an ablation, robustness test or supplementary experiment.

E5.justification: Five-trial averaging for Figure 1 moves from v1 Appendix B.1 to v2 Section 5.1. No additional seed information, uncertainty estimates or statistical tests are reported.

E6.justification: All empirical panels in Figures 1–3 are identical across versions, preserving the runtime, MSE and reconstruction-error results. The newly discussed lower MSE around ALS step 15 was already displayed in v1 Figure 1.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds definitions of fully connected, ring and wheel tensor-network topologies through their connectivity. The lifting lemmas, Theorem 3.7, assumptions, runtime corollaries and proof arguments remain unchanged; the proofs move to Appendix B.

C1.justification: The central claims about lifting, approximate Richardson convergence, CP/Tucker/TT completion and possible 100x speedups are retained. The contribution summary now explicitly mentions the already-present coupled-matrix demonstration.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 newly explains the coupled-matrix MSE behavior through stochastic approximation and different convergence paths. The introduction clarifies conditional applicability to regularized objectives, while Appendix A.4 discusses extensions to additional decomposition families.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in Section 5 but drops v1 Appendix B.1's statement that the sampling algorithm runs for seven iterations. NumPy/TensorLy, Apple M2 hardware, 8 GB RAM and the other experimental details are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds seven cited works covering fully connected networks, tensor rings, tensor wheels and t-product decompositions, explaining connections to the lifting approach. The main related-work positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: Section 3 proofs move to Appendix B, tensor-train sampling details move to Appendix C, and the coupled-matrix appendix material moves into Section 5.1. Experimental appendices are reorganized, with additional explanatory prose and acknowledgements.

P2.justification: The main paper and references change from single-column presentation to a two-column conference layout, with extensive equation and figure reflow. Figure 1 is substantially reduced in size and Figure 2 gains an expanded caption; all four figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves usability through a code-access link, a more self-contained experimental narrative, clearer figure explanations and broader applicability discussion. The central theory and empirical evidence are retained. Losing the seven-iteration disclosure and shrinking Figure 1 partly offset these gains.
